summary: Robot-agnostic AI models and interfaces for intelligent machines.
editor_note: The bottleneck in robotics may be the interface, not the arm. A foundation-model stack, hardware abstraction, and browser controls already put two live robot experiences behind visible queues. Unlike a hardware company optimizing one form factor, the bet is that intelligence and interaction should travel across machines. The open question is whether a three-day public demo becomes a durable deployment product.

product_evidence.claim: Enigma describes a stack of foundation robotics models, a robot-agnostic abstraction, and a human interface intended to work across warehouse arms, humanoids, and other form factors without rebuilding for each platform.
Robots.online exposes browser-based live robot interactions: The Painter and The Duelist were queueable, while The Laborant was marked offline and coming soon at verification.
The product terms describe browser sessions with real-time robot feeds, prompts or controls, and session recordings, with interaction data reusable for product improvement and model training.

market_context.primary_user: Robotics engineers, enterprises, and product teams evaluating intelligent behavior and interfaces across heterogeneous robot hardware.
market_context.differentiation: A full-stack approach combining robotics foundation models, a robot-agnostic adaptation layer, and human interfaces with a public live-interaction feedback loop.
market_context.why_now: The July 2026 $71M Seed round coincides with a public live-control surface, making the financing signal and product-evaluation evidence observable at the same time.

risks.claim: Whether the claimed no-rebuild-per-platform behavior generalizes beyond staged browser demos remains unproven and can be tested through public benchmarks or named heterogeneous-hardware deployments.
risks.basis: The official site makes the cross-form-factor claim, while the public product exposed two queueable experiences and one offline or coming-soon experience.
